messages:
maria: FYI customer 'Papaya' hitting intermittent 502/504s on hosted API since ~09:10 UTC. They see failures spike when their clients rotate tokens (~every 30s). Attaching sample curl and trace ids. Can SRE triage?

maria: curl -v \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}'

maria: trace ids: tx=abc123, tx=def456, tx=ghi789 (these are from the client logs)

sam_sre: on it. Is this only for that tenant or multiple customers?

maria: only Papaya so far (they were a heavy embedder earlier today). They reported ~6% 5xx over last 10m, p95 latency jumped too.

sam_sre: quick ask: can you grab one of the failing request IDs (x-request-id) and the edge proxy log line? also envoy admin /stats and cluster dump would help: 
```
curl -sS http://edge-proxy:9901/stats | grep auth_upstream
curl -sS http://edge-proxy:9901/clusters?format=json > /tmp/clusters.json
```

maria: pasted the log snippet: 
```
[2025-02-12T09:12:41Z] proxy edge: request_id=tx=abc123 upstream=auth-upstream status=504 dispatch_ms=1203 conn_pool_exhausted
```

sam_sre: good — conn_pool_exhausted is the clue. Looks like the h2 conn pool to auth-upstream is saturated during token refresh bursts. Did we roll any auth-proxy change in last hour?

deploy-bot: rolled back auth-proxy config change (id: cfg-1723) at 2025-02-12T09:05:00Z by ops-deploy. No other deploys in window.

devin_eng: I can reproduce locally with a small script that rotates headers and keeps ~50 concurrent connections. Try this to reproduce quickly: 
```
# repro: hammer auth path while rotating token header
for i in {1..200}; do 
  TOKEN=$(cat /dev/urandom | tr -dc 'a-z0-9' | head -c8)
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\\n" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\" &
  sleep 0.02
done
```

sam_sre: thanks. From metrics: h2.active_streams and cluster.conn_pool_exhaustion counter spike at same time. Auth upstream cluster has circuit-breakers default low (max_connections: 2). That explains 504s when many token validation calls are attempted in parallel.

devin_eng: sketch of fix: bump auth cluster max_connections and max_requests_per_connection, and enable per-host circuit breakers higher for this tenant. Also add short in-process token cache (100ms TTL) to reduce outbound auth calls for rotations.

sam_sre: short mitigation: increase h2 conn pool to 8 on auth cluster and add adaptive backoff in auth client. I'll open a quick patch and roll to canary.

maria: can you also suggest a temporary customer-facing mitigation we can ask Papaya to apply?

alice_csm: told customer to reduce client concurrency to <=5 and enable exponential backoff for retries. Offered to move them to a dedicated capacity pool for a week while we stabilize. They want to try the client changes first. :+1:

sam_sre: patch opened: env cluster change (cluster: auth-upstream): 
```
circuit_breakers:
  thresholds:
    - max_connections: 8
      max_pending_requests: 100
      max_requests: 0
      max_retries: 3
```
Rolling canary to 10% now.

deploy-bot: started canary rollout for config cfg-1748 -> 10% at 2025-02-12T09:28:00Z

sam_sre: monitoring... auth_conn_pool_exhaustion counter dropped to near zero after canary. 5xx rate for Papaya down to 0.8% over 5m. p95 latency recovering.

devin_eng: followups: add token-cache with 200ms TTL in auth client, add jitter to retries on client side, and instrument per-tenant token churn metric. I'll file tickets and assign.

maria: great, thanks everyone. I'll update Papaya and close the escalation once they confirm stability.

alice_csm: customer confirmed reduced errors after client change; asked for postmortem and whether we can proactively detect conn_pool_exhaustion and autoscale the auth cluster.

sam_sre: agree — adding alert on conn_pool_exhaustion and a runbook. I'll draft the postmortem with timeline and mitigation steps.

maria: awesome. closing loop later today. :white_check_mark:
